newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open stronger on gains in U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open stronger on gains in U.S. market.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened mostly stronger in moderate trade on Thursday, with the market taking much of its direction from gains in U.S. Treasuries, analysts said.

"It's the still strong U.S. market. This rally in the U.S. is still pressing higher much to my surprise. I would say that most technical traders are agreeing that the market is overbought," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.33 to C$116.13 to yield 6.739 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.68 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to six basis points from seven basis points at Wednesday's close.
Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened on Thursday morning following an unexpected rise in U.S. jobless claims data.
In Canada, the government reported that retail sales rose by a stronger-than-expected 1.1 percent in April from March and April's trade surplus was a lower than expected C$1.72 billion.
Analysts said the market largely disregarded the Canadian numbers and focused instead on U.S. trading activity.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.11 to C$107.88 to yield 6.176 percent, while the U.S. 10-year traded unchanged to yield 6.40 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 22 basis points from 21 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.84 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.07 percent.
